recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-17426 unless the work group opens a new issue to define broader non-query or push semantics for SUBSETTED.
issue_request: FHIR-17426 asked whether SUBSETTED should be described as useful in push scenarios, not only query _summary. The final Published resolution was Not Persuasive with Modification: it rejected broad push guidance, said PATCH is the only safe way to pass a record without all data when minimizing volume is the objective, and required focused guidance for POST/PUT requests tagged SUBSETTED, the safety checklist, and updates.html.
initial_application: No correctly tagged FHIR-17426 implementation commit was found. Commit 7ad9e8aa04cfb006e56bbb40316234270869e91b, dated 2022-02-21 and titled FHIR#17462, changed source/http.html, source/safety.html, and source/updates.html in exactly the way FHIR-17426 requested; FHIR-17462 itself is an unrelated marital-status-code-system issue, so that commit appears to have a transposed Jira key. Later source history preserved and refined this application.
additional_context: FHIR-32757 later removed the incorrect SUBSETTED Security Label sentence from updates.html while preserving the server-discretion guidance. FHIR-22500 reconciliation mirrored the SUBSETTED safety checklist item into the active safety-entries CodeSystem, and FHIR-20672 corrected adjacent REST SUBSETTED tag terminology. A 2021 Zulip thread supported cautious create/update handling for SUBSETTED-tagged resources, and FHIR-I Confluence minutes match the Jira feedback and final vote path.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/http.html warns on update and create that servers decide whether to accept SUBSETTED-tagged requests and how to handle them; source/updates.html covers the same server discretion plus accidental data-loss and invalidation risks; source/safety.html and the active safety-entries CodeSystem include the limited-access SUBSETTED update/create checklist item.
